chunks: Converting between number bases. The question: Convert some binary/hex/oct/decimal number to a different base.
A number base is how many different digits a counting system uses. Decimal uses 10 digits, binary uses 2 (0 and 1), and hexadecimal (hex) uses 16 (0 to 9, then A to F).
Converting between bases changes how a number is written, not how big it is. Hardware stores everything in binary, but people find hex shorter to read.
Suppose you must pay 13 cents. With coins worth 1, 10 and 100 you pay one 10 and three 1 seconds, which is the decimal "13".
With coins worth 1, 2, 4 and 8 you pay one 8, one 4 and one 1, which is binary 1101. The amount is the same, and only the coin set changes.
The same 16 bits grouped two ways.
Hex groups of four from the right give B, E, E, F; octal groups of three from the right give 1, 3, 7, 3, 5, 7 (the leftmost group has just one bit, padded with zeros).
Because both groupings start at the right-hand end (the LSB), the number needs no arithmetic to convert: 0xBEEF = 0o137357.
Base (radix): how many different digits the system has, such as 2, 10 or 16. Place value: the worth of a digit's position. In binary the places are 1, 2, 4, 8, and so on.
Bit and nibble: a bit is one binary digit. A nibble is 4 bits, which is exactly one hex digit. Hex digits A to F: stand for 10 to 15, so a single character holds a value up to 15.
Convert 175 to binary. Pick the largest place values that fit: 128 + 32 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 175. That puts a 1 in those places and a 0 in the others, which gives 1010 1111.
For hex, split the bits into groups of four from the right. 1010 is 10, written A, and 1111 is 15, written F. So 175 is 0xAF, and as a check, 10 times 16 plus 15 equals 175 .
"Every base is positional, so to get to decimal I add digit times power of the base: 0xAF is 10 times 16 plus 15, which is 175.
Going from decimal, I divide repeatedly by the target base and read the remainders bottom to top.
For binary to hex or octal I just group the bits, 4 per hex digit and 3 per octal digit, starting from the right: 1010 1111 is AF, and 10 101 111 is 257 in octal.
Then I check by converting back."
